guideTitle: 6 Best Door Knob Grips Under $15 in 2026
metaTitle: Best Door Knob Grips Under $15 in 2026
metaDescription: Six budget door knob grips compared: a six-piece ribbed Eggone set, Enjoy Cover two-packs and doorstop covers, plus the Able Life EZ sleeve.
introParagraphs: Stepping up from the lowest cap brings in the first multi-door set. The Eggone six-piece pack changes the math for a whole house, because you can cover every round knob at once instead of buying one or two covers at a time. Everything here is still a stretchy silicone sleeve, though, so the questions that matter are the same: does it fit your knob, does it add a doorstop bumper, and how many doors do you have. Because all six are cheap, spend your attention on measuring the knob rather than on tiny differences in brand.

We evaluated six distinct listings: the Eggone six-piece ribbed silicone set, the Enjoy Cover two-pack of non-slip grips, the Enjoy Cover upgraded ergonomic two-pack, the Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips, the Enjoy Cover single-pack doorstop grip and the Enjoy Cover doorstop grip cover. Judgments rest on listed sizes, materials, pack counts and extras, plus where listings overlap.

What this cap still cannot do is change the shape of the handle. For a hand that cannot close around a knob, a lever replacement is the real fix, and a cover only improves friction. We make no medical claims about any of these products. At this level the only pick that changes the coverage math is the six-piece Eggone, and the only picks that change how a door behaves against the wall are the two Enjoy Cover doorstop listings.

products.name: Eggone 6 Pcs Silicone Door Knob Grips
products.description:
Eggone sells six silicone grips, each listed at 3 inches wide and 2 inches deep, with a ribbed texture and a glow insert for finding the knob in a dark room. The listing calls the material silica gel that is chemically stable and durable, and says it makes round knobs easier to turn and offers a better grip for weaker or older hands. Six pieces covers a typical home's interior doors in one order.

The ribbing is the key detail: it gives fingers something to bite on that a smooth sleeve does not. The 3 by 2 inch size is a single stated number, so check that your knob fits within it, since a large knob may not stretch. The glow insert is a small extra, though the listing does not say how bright or long-lasting it is.

To use it, stretch it on by hand. Next to the Enjoy Cover two-pack that covers two doors, the Eggone covers six, which is the main reason it leads this lineup for a whole house. It is not a doorstop and has no wall bumper. Six covers also means you can keep two spare for the knobs that see the most traffic, such as the bathroom and the back door. A set this size is the one in the lineup where cost per door is clearly lowest, which is the real value argument at this cap. It is also the only pick whose listing states a width and depth, so it is the easiest to sanity check with a tape measure.
products.bestFor: Covering every round knob in a home with a ribbed, textured grip.
pros: Six pieces cover a whole home
Glow insert helps in dim rooms
Stated 3 x 2 in size lets you check fit
cons: Single stated size, large knobs may not fit

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Upgraded Ergonomic Door Knob Grips
products.description:
The upgraded Enjoy Cover two-pack is soft non-slip silicone shaped to make a knob easier to take hold of. The listing says the covers are compatible with most standard round knobs and stretch to accommodate different sizes while keeping a firm hold. Installation needs no tools, just a stretch and slip over the existing knob.

The word upgraded is not explained in the highlights, so check the product page for what changed. Two covers cover two doors, which is less than the Eggone's six. There is no wall bumper.

Compared with the standard Enjoy Cover two-pack, this one is the newer design from the same brand. If you want a branded, ergonomic option for two doors, it is a clean choice. The brand listing stresses an ergonomic shape that makes the knob easier to grasp, but gives no thickness figure, so it is hard to compare with the Eggone at 3 by 2 inches. Two covers is a sensible count for a bathroom and a bedroom. Choose it over the six-piece set if you want fewer, branded pieces.
products.bestFor: Two doors where you want the brand's newer ergonomic shape.

products.name: Enjoy Cover 2 Pack Silicone Door Knob Grips
products.description:
This is the standard Enjoy Cover two-pack, made of 100 percent silicone that the listing says is non-toxic, BPA free and allergy free. It claims one size fits most standard knobs and installs in seconds with no tools. It washes with soap and water, which keeps the surface grippy.

It has no bumper, so it is the plain sleeve of the family. Two covers is a small count compared with the Eggone. The listing says it meets all safety standards, which is a general claim to verify on the page.

It works the same way as the upgraded version, so the choice between them is mostly about preference. If you want a simple, washable pair with no extras, it is the good default. The listing also mentions it is easy to clean with water and soap, which the upgraded version does not repeat. On paper the surface should feel the same as the upgraded cover. At two covers it is better value for a small flat than for a family home.
products.bestFor: A washable plain sleeve pair for two doors.
pros: Non-toxic, BPA free per the listing

products.name: Enjoy Cover Doorstop Door Handle Grip, Single Pack
products.description:
This single-pack Enjoy Cover is an all-in-one cover with a soft bumper that stops the knob hitting the wall. The listing says it provides a secure non-slip grip, wall protection and an ergonomic design. It covers one door.

The bumper adds bulk on one side, so it feels different from a plain sleeve. It is sold singly, so a house with many doors needs many packs. The patent pending note is about the design, not performance.

Against the Eggone's six pieces, this gives one cover with a function the Eggone lacks. If one door bangs the wall, it is the right pick. The bumper is soft silicone, so it should not mark paint, though a hard impact will still dent plaster behind it. For a child room door that is regularly flung open, it protects the wall and gives a better grip in one piece. For a hallway with no wall behind the door, a plain sleeve is simpler.
products.bestFor: A single door that slams into a wall.
pros: One cover for one problem door

products.name: Enjoy Cover Doorstop Silicone Door Handle Grip Cover
products.description:
This listing describes the original ergonomic doorstop grip, a door knob protector and wall stopper in one. It lists anti-slip silicone, wall protection and an ergonomic design aimed at people with limited hand strength. The look is similar to the single pack, so confirm the pack size.

The doorstop bumper is its main feature. It has the same bulk trade-off. If you read this listing and want the original-branded version, this is it.

Compared with the Able Life sleeve, it adds a bumper. It is a good pick if wall protection matters. Because it is sold as the original, it is the one to pick if you have seen the product in a store. If the page shows a two-pack option, compare it with the two-pack listings above before buying a single. It is a sound choice where wall protection is the problem.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want the original doorstop design.

products.name: Able Life EZ Doorknob Grips
products.description:
Able Life offers non-slip silicone covers that stretch over a door knob, listed as a knob turner and handle gripper. The listing says it opens doors effortlessly, costs less than a door-lever replacement and installs easily. It is the only non-Enjoy Cover, non-Eggone brand here.

The listing gives few specifics, so confirm size and pack. There is no bumper. If you prefer a different brand, it is a plain, simple option.

It works by stretching, with no tools. Compared with the Eggone six-pack, it gives less detail and probably fewer pieces. The lack of detail also means you should read the questions on the page before ordering. If your knob is a standard round shape, it should work as a plain sleeve. Compared with the Enjoy Cover two-pack, it gives you a third brand to try if the others do not fit.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a plain sleeve from a third brand.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Fit is the first filter, because a sleeve that does not match the knob will spin or tear. The Eggone lists 3 inches wide by 2 inches deep, while the Enjoy Cover two-packs say they fit most standard round knobs and stretch to different sizes. Measure your knob across the widest point and depth, then compare with the product page. Large decorative knobs and small cabinet knobs are the usual failures. If your knob is outside the range, none of these will help.

Texture gives fingers purchase, and it is the cheapest way to improve grip. The Eggone has a ribbed texture described as comfortable on older hands, and the Enjoy Cover listings describe soft non-slip silicone. A ribbed sleeve works better on lotioned or damp hands. Choose ribbing if smooth silicone slides under your fingers, and smooth if you prefer a slim feel. Wipe the surface regularly to keep friction.

A bumper protects the wall behind the door at the price of bulk on one side. Two Enjoy Cover listings include a soft bumper, while the Eggone, the two-packs and the Able Life are plain sleeves. Check whether your door actually hits the wall, because a bumper on a free-swinging door is wasted. Position matters, since the bumper must face the wall. A bumper can also stop a door slamming against a surface in a child room.

Coverage per pack decides value. The Eggone gives six pieces, the Enjoy Cover two-packs two each, and the doorstop and Able Life listings are single or unclear. Count the knobs that matter for daily use, typically bathroom, bedroom and entry. A house of eight round knobs needs the Eggone plus a couple more. Buying a single doorstop for each door gets expensive fast.

The Eggone adds glow inserts so you can find the knob in a dark hallway. The listing does not state how bright they are or how long they last. Do not rely on them like a night light. They are most useful in a bedroom or bathroom you visit at night. Check the page for how the insert is mounted.

A cover does not change the shape of the handle, and that matters more than most buyers expect. The Able Life listing itself says its grips cost less than a lever replacement, which is honest about the trade. Levers need less hand closure and can be pushed with a wrist, which covers cannot offer. Add-on lever extensions can stress the latch, so check any fit carefully. Start with a cover, then consider a lever if the knob remains hard.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip texture
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated surface detail. The Eggone leads with a ribbed texture, followed by the Enjoy Cover non-slip silicone. The Able Life gives the least detail. Based on product specs. The Enjoy Cover upgraded listing mentions an ergonomic shape, while the doorstop listings combine grip and bumper. None lists a measured friction figure.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit information
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated sizes. The Eggone lists 3 by 2 inches, and the Enjoy Cover two-packs say most standard round knobs. Others gave less. We treated a missing range as unconfirmed rather than assuming a universal fit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Extras
howWeEvaluated.description: We noted the Enjoy Cover doorstop bumper and the Eggone glow insert as the two extras in the lineup. The bumper and glow insert are described by their makers only, so we give no performance rating.

howWeEvaluated.title: Coverage per pack
howWeEvaluated.description: Six pieces in the Eggone lead on coverage. Two-packs cover two doors, and the doorstop and Able Life listings are the smallest. The Eggone is the best coverage per order, and the single-pack doorstop is the narrowest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ease of use
howWeEvaluated.description: All stretch on without tools. The Enjoy Cover two-pack adds washing with soap and water. Removal is just a stretch, the reverse of installation.

faq.q: Which is best for a whole house?
faq.a: The Eggone six-piece set, because six covers handle most interior doors in one order. The Enjoy Cover two-packs cover only two. Check your knob size against the 3 by 2 inch listing. A house with eight knobs would still need a second pack.

faq.q: Does the Eggone glow in the dark?
faq.a: The listing mentions glow inserts. It does not give brightness or duration. Treat it as a small extra and check the product page. Check the product page for the exact fit of the glow insert.
The two Enjoy Cover doorstop listings. The Eggone, two-packs and Able Life do not. The bumper adds bulk. Pick the doorstop listings only if the door actually swings into a wall.
Maybe not. The Eggone lists 3 by 2 inches. The Enjoy Cover says most standard sizes. Measure before buying. Measure twice, because a loose cover is worse than none.

faq.q: Are they a substitute for a lever handle?
faq.a: No, a common misconception. They add friction only. A lever needs less hand closure. A knob that needs a firm closed fist will still be hard to turn even with the sleeve.
The Enjoy Cover two-pack says soap and water. Silicone wipes clean. Check the others. Do not use harsh cleaners that could degrade the silicone.

The Enjoy Cover two-pack describes non-toxic, BPA free silicone, and the Eggone says its silica gel is chemically stable. A sleeve should not be treated as a childproofing device, since a grip cover makes a knob easier, not harder, to turn. If you want to keep a child away from a door, a separate door lock is a different product. Check the product page for age notes.

faq.q: How long do silicone covers last?
faq.a: They are stretchy, so expect them to loosen slowly with use and heat. Wash and dry them occasionally, and replace a cover that no longer grips the knob firmly. The Eggone six-piece count helps here because you have spares. None of the listings gives a lifespan, so treat durability as unconfirmed.
